$comment: §20.2's safety boundaries, and what covers each one. The list is NOT written here: it is read out of the case study at check time, because a list transcribed into this file would be checked against my own copy rather than against the requirement. What is written here is the claim about each boundary - a check that must have run, or an issue that owes it.

source.$comment: Where the boundaries come from, and how they are found. A boundary added to the case study appears here with nothing claiming it, and the suite fails until something does.
source.shape: a bullet list, one boundary per line
source.atLeastReason: What §20.2 listed when this was written. A floor, not a count: adding a boundary must not fail, and removing one must not pass. Without it, deleting a boundary together with its claim slips through - staleClaims only sees a claim whose boundary is gone, not a pair that left together. Lowering this number is how someone says out loud that a safety requirement was dropped.

claims.$comment: Keyed by the boundary's text as the case study writes it. Each names either checks that must have run - as "suite:check name", because a bare name can appear in more than one suite and a boundary would then be covered by whichever check happened to share a name - or an owner who owes it. Never both, and never neither.

test:failure:during_publish: a cancel between candidates is honoured by name
test:failure:a cancelled attempt releases the name it reserved too
